liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Keep Your Day Job** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer finds this closer lackluster, with Garcia flagging after a tight start; Listed as the encore, following Sugar Magnolia [2][12]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer calls it lackluster, as Garcia's playing and voice had declined late in set two [12]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the fastest version ever, placed unusually after Bertha in set one [17]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer singles out this song as a highlight [19]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed the Iko Iko show opener [21]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer praises the Mississippi Half-Step into Franklin's Tower pairing [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd86-02-08 s0 t01 Chinese Symphony Orchestra**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t02 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t03 Iko Iko**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t04 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t05 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t06 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t07 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-08 s1 t08 It's All Over Now**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-02-08.140205.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 147 min [1]
- **gd1986-02-08.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.106033.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 129 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1986-02-08.142388.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 128 min [4]
- **gd1986-02-08.142381.dts.tobin.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 128 min [5]
- **gd1986-02-08.senn441.padelimike.83804.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 127 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [7]
- **gd86-02-08.sbd.ladner.20724.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 120 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard recording good quality; Reviewer describes the soundboard as sparkling in quality; Reviewer's old poor-generation first-set tape contrasts with this recording, which sounds excellent [10][12][17]
- **gd86-02-08.beyer.connor.2987.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 124 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the audience recording as very good [13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls it the opening night of a five-night run at the Kaiser [11]
- Chinese New Year and Mardi Gras brought extra festive touches to the night [11]
- Reviewer was 16 and flew in from New York City for this show [14]
- Reviewer recalls the Kaiser's basement bar as the best of any venue then, with intense energy [16]
- The Chinese Symphony Orchestra opened the show for Chinese New Year [1]
- Reviewer's first West Coast shows; says East Coast shows had nothing like this [11]
- Reviewer notes that Half-Step going into Franklin's Tower was rare, making this show unique [17]
